Subject: Draft Mutual Action Plan: proposed milestones & stakeholders for Meditech POC

Hi Amit / Renee —

Thanks again for the discovery call today — great conversation and helpful context on your performance targets and compliance needs. As promised, I attached an initial Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that captures the milestones we discussed, suggested owners from both sides, and two timeline options (aggressive vs conservative) so you can pick what fits your internal cadence. Attachment stubs: (Meditech_MAP_v0.1.xlsx) and discovery notes (Discovery-Notes-20260915.pdf).

Summary highlights in the MAP (please see sheet "Summary"):
- Goal: 6-week POC to validate integration and latency/cost targets for the patient-data normalization pipeline. Target outcome: prototype integration + basic throughput tests.
- Milestones: 1) Environment access & network allowlist (Meditech) 2) Private connector & test data load (joint) 3) Initial inference baseline & latency tuning (Redwood) 4) Stability run & cost estimate (joint) 5) Executive review & go/no-go (Meditech + Redwood)
- Proposed owners: Meditech: IT Network (Renee) for allowlisting; Data Engineering (Amit) for test data; Redwood: Solutions Eng (Sean) for connector setup; Account Exec (Vanessa) for timeline and procurement coordination.
- Dependencies: KMS key access, cert for private endpoint, test dataset subset sanitized, SOC 2 evidence requested by Meditech security (we captured in discovery notes).
- Target close for POC decision: two options in MAP: Oct 30 (aggressive) or Nov 17 (conservative).

Please review the draft and reply with: 1) which timeline you prefer (Oct 30 or Nov 17), 2) any other internal stakeholders to include (security, procurement, legal), and 3) any missing dependencies we should add. If these look broadly correct, I will convert the sheet to a shared MAP and set milestones in a shared Drive link and in HubSpot (I included the HubSpot placeholder).

Next steps on our side once you confirm timeline:
- I will provision a private MAP folder and invite the stakeholders you confirm.
- Sean will coordinate a follow-up technical kickoff (30–45 min) to confirm access paths and test data format.
- We will provide a short checklist for procurement so your procurement team has the licensing and SLA information up front.

Thanks — appreciate the quick read. If easier, share times and I can set a brief follow-up to finalize stakeholders.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and for pulling this together. The MAP structure looks good and captures the key steps. A few quick items from our side:

1) Timeline: we prefer the conservative option (Nov 17). We have an internal vendor security review week of Oct 19 that might delay earlier tasks.
2) Stakeholders to add: Legal (K. Morales legal@meditech.com) and Procurement (T. Huang procurement@meditech.com). Security lead is internal but point of contact will be Renee for allowlist / cert coordination.
3) Dependencies: please add the expected format and schema for redaction markers in the test dataset (we need to review), and note that we require an international data-processing addendum if any processing leaves the US region.

Also, could Sean share a brief checklist of what network ports and cert types are required? I can get IT to prepare the allowlist but want to give them the exact details.

I reviewed the SOC 2 evidence note — procurement will want to see proof of logging retention and audit entries; can we include a short note about default retention and how audit logs are exported?

I'll loop K. Morales and T. Huang once we have the shared MAP in Drive.

Appreciate the clear next steps.

Thanks,
Amit
Head of Data Engineering | Meditech Health
